```{r, include=FALSE}
library(highcharter)
hc_set_theme("hcrt", tooltip = list(valueDecimals = 2))
options(download.file.method = "libcurl")
```

`hchart()` chooses a chart based on the class of its input. Find your object
type below, then use the `hc_*` functions to customize the resulting chart.

## Data objects

### Data frames

This function works like `qplot`: You pass the data, choose the type
of chart and then define the aesthetics for each variable.

```{r}
library(highcharter)
library(dplyr)

data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")
data(diamonds, economics_long, package = "ggplot2")

hchart(
  penguins,
  "scatter",
  hcaes(x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm, group = species)
)

penguins2 <- penguins |>
  count(species, island) |>
  glimpse()

hchart(penguins2, "column", hcaes(x = island, y = n, group = species))
```

Check automatically if the x column is date class:

```{r}
economics_long2 <- economics_long |>
  filter(variable %in% c("pop", "uempmed", "unemploy"))

hchart(economics_long2, "line", hcaes(x = date, y = value01, group = variable))
```

### Numeric & histograms

```{r}
set.seed(123)
x <- rgamma(1000, shape = 2)
hchart(x)
```

### Densities

```{r}
hchart(density(x), type = "area", color = "#B71C1C", name = "Gamma sample")
```

### Empirical cumulative distributions

The height at each x-value is the fraction of the sample at or below it.
For example, `r sum(x <= 2)` of the 1,000 observations are at or below 2.

```{r hchart-ecdf}
hchart(ecdf(x), name = "Gamma sample")
```

### Precomputed histograms

Pass a histogram object when you want R to choose the breaks before charting.
The bin boundaries and counts are preserved.

```{r precomputed-histogram}
hchart(hist(x, breaks = 30, plot = FALSE), name = "Gamma sample")
```

### Character & factor

```{r}
x <- diamonds$cut
hchart(x, type = "column")
```

### Frequency tables

Each cell shows how many cars have that combination of cylinders and gears.
Zero counts remain visible in the heatmap. For a one-way table, see
[Category order](highcharts-api.html#category-order).

```{r hchart-table}
hchart(table(Cylinders = mtcars$cyl, Gears = mtcars$gear))
```

### Matrix

```{css, echo=FALSE}
.volcano-grid { container-type: inline-size; }
.volcano-grid .highchart {
  --legend-width: 96px;
  --grid-width: min(calc(100cqi - var(--legend-width)), 26rem);
  width: calc(var(--grid-width) + var(--legend-width)) !important;
  height: calc(var(--grid-width) * var(--rows) / var(--cols)) !important;
  margin-inline: auto;
}
```

The `volcano` matrix has 87 rows and 61 columns. Both views use the same
distance for one step across a column or down a row.

```{r volcano-layout}
data(volcano)

volcano_layout <- function(chart) {
  chart |>
    hc_chart(margin = c(0, 96, 0, 0)) |>
    hc_legend(layout = "vertical", align = "right", verticalAlign = "middle")
}
```

::: {.volcano-grid style="--rows: 87; --cols: 61;"}

```{r volcano-heatmap}
# fmt: skip
volcano_colors <- c("#000004", "#56106E", "#BB3754", "#F98C0A", "#FCFFA4")

hchart(volcano) |>
  volcano_layout() |>
  hc_colorAxis(stops = color_stops(colors = volcano_colors))
```

:::

The elevations in `volcano` are whole metres. Place contour lines half a metre
above each multiple of ten so that flat areas keep their band color. Blue,
yellow and coral mark increasing elevation, as in the
[Highcharts contour demo](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-and-series-types/contour).
This view requires WebGPU in the browser.

::: {.volcano-grid style="--rows: 86; --cols: 60;"}

```{r matrix-grid-types}
hchart(
  volcano,
  type = "contour",
  contourInterval = 10,
  contourOffset = 0.5,
  lineColor = "#888888"
) |>
  volcano_layout() |>
  hc_colorAxis(
    min = min(volcano),
    max = max(volcano),
    startOnTick = FALSE,
    endOnTick = FALSE,
    stops = color_stops(3, c("#447CFF", "#F5FF66", "#FF5E4F")),
    labels = list(format = "{value} m")
  )
```

:::

### Distance matrix

```{r}
mtcars2 <- mtcars[1:20, ]
x <- dist(mtcars2)
hchart(x)
```

### Correlation matrix

```{r}
hchart(cor(mtcars))
```

### Principal components

Each point represents one state. Axis titles give the share of variance
explained by each component. Hover over a point to see the state's name.

Use `loadings = TRUE` to show how the variables relate to the chosen
components. Use `scale = 0` for the raw observation scores.

```{r hchart-pca-loadings}
fit <- prcomp(USArrests, scale. = TRUE)
hchart(fit, choices = c(1, 3), loadings = TRUE)
```

### GeoJSON

```{r, child="_manchester.Rmd"}
```

The [Maps vignette](maps.html#laguna-seca) shows how to style these geometry
types separately on a racing circuit.

## Time series

```{r}
hchart(LakeHuron, name = "Level") |>
  hc_title(text = "Level of Lake Huron 1875–1972")
```

### Multivariate time series

```{r}
x <- cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths)
hchart(x)
```

### Seasonal decomposition

The four panels share a time axis and show the observed series, seasonality,
trend and remainder. Gaps at the ends of the trend are part of the fitted
decomposition.

```{r hchart-decompose}
hchart(stats::decompose(AirPassengers, type = "multiplicative"))
```

### Seasonal decomposition of time series by loess

```{r}
x <- stl(log(AirPassengers), "per")
hchart(x)
```

### Seasonal adjustment with X-13

With the optional `seasonal` package installed, compare the original monthly
series with the X-13-adjusted series on the same scale. Labels mark the outliers
reported by the model at the adjusted value, as in `plot(fit)` (e.g., AO for
an additive outlier or LS for a level shift).

```{r x13, eval=requireNamespace("seasonal", quietly=TRUE)}
fit <- seasonal::seas(AirPassengers)
hchart(fit)
```

### Forecast package

The legend distinguishes the observed series from the forecast. Prediction
intervals are linked to the forecast series. Supply `name` to label the subject;
the chart adds the observed/forecast suffixes.

```{r}
library(forecast)

x <- forecast(ets(USAccDeaths), h = 48, level = 95)
hchart(x)
```

### Exponential-smoothing components

An `ets` model shows its observed values and fitted level, slope or seasonal
states in aligned panels. To show future values instead, pass the model to
`forecast()` and chart the resulting forecast object.

```{r ets-components}
hchart(forecast::ets(AirPassengers))
```

### Autocovariance & autocorrelation

```{r}
changes <- diff(AirPassengers)
hchart(acf(changes, plot = FALSE))
hchart(pacf(changes, plot = FALSE))
```

With two monthly series, the diagonal panels show each series' autocorrelation.
The other two panels show their cross-correlation at positive and negative
lags. The horizontal axes use years, the time unit of these monthly series.

```{r multivariate-acf}
hchart(acf(cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths), lag.max = 12, plot = FALSE))
```

### Quantmod package

The highstock extension is used to chart `xts` and `xts ohlc` classes from the
quantmod package.

```{r}
library(quantmod)

data(sample_matrix, package = "xts")
x <- xts::as.xts(sample_matrix)

hchart(x)
```

## Fitted models

### Random forests

The overall out-of-bag error and the class-specific errors show how quickly
the forest stabilizes. Hover at a tree count to compare the overall and
per-species errors in one table.

```{r forest-error, eval=requireNamespace("randomForest", quietly=TRUE)}
set.seed(42)
forest <- randomForest::randomForest(Species ~ ., data = iris, ntree = 150)
hchart(forest)
```

For variable importance, chart the mean decrease in Gini impurity from the same fit.

```{r forest-importance, eval=requireNamespace("randomForest", quietly=TRUE)}
gini <- randomForest::importance(forest, type = 2)
importance <- data.frame(feature = rownames(gini), decrease = as.numeric(gini))
importance <- importance[order(importance$decrease, decreasing = TRUE), ]
hchart(
  importance,
  "bar",
  hcaes(x = feature, y = decrease),
  name = "Mean decrease in Gini"
)
```

### Cross-validated regularization

Each point shows mean cross-validated prediction error. Its whiskers extend
one standard error in either direction. The two vertical lines identify the
best-scoring lambda and the more regularized one-standard-error choice.
Move the horizontal crosshair to an interval endpoint to see which other
intervals reach that value.

```{r glmnet-error, eval=requireNamespace("glmnet", quietly=TRUE)}
x <- as.matrix(mtcars[c("disp", "hp", "wt", "qsec")])
set.seed(42)
folds <- sample(rep_len(1:5, nrow(x)))
cv <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(x, mtcars$mpg, foldid = folds)
hchart(cv)
```

### Survival package

Survival models can be charted.

```{r}
library(survival)

data(cancer, package = "survival")

lung <- dplyr::mutate(cancer, sex = ifelse(sex == 1, "Male", "Female"))

fit <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ sex, data = cancer)

hchart(fit, ranges = TRUE)
```

## Decision trees

Node area shows how many training observations reach each split or leaf.
For classification, select a donut or a bar to see the class proportions.
For regression, the node color follows the mean response. Hover over a node
for its summary, or click a split to fold the subtree.

```{r decision-tree, eval=requireNamespace("partykit", quietly=TRUE)}
fit <- partykit::ctree(Species ~ Petal.Length + Petal.Width, data = iris)
hchart(fit, node_shape = "bar") |>
  hc_colors(c("#087B71", "#AD591D", "#7655A0"))
```

### Boosted trees

Select a tree by its one-based index. Hover over a split for its gain and the
direction taken by missing values, or over a leaf for its margin contribution.
Marker size follows cover.

```{r xgb-tree, eval=requireNamespace("xgboost", quietly=TRUE) && packageVersion("xgboost") >= "3.1.0"}
x <- as.matrix(iris[c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", "Petal.Length")])
d <- xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(x, label = iris$Petal.Width)
fit <- xgboost::xgb.train(
  list(objective = "reg:squarederror", max_depth = 2L, nthread = 1L),
  d,
  nrounds = 3L,
  verbose = 0
)
hchart(fit, tree = 2)
```

## Dendrograms and phylogenies

### Cluster dendrograms

The vertical position of each join gives the merge height. Hover over it for
the number of observations. Both `hchart(fit)` and
`hchart(as.dendrogram(fit))` use the same layout.

```{r cluster-dendrogram}
states <- scale(USArrests[
  c(
    "Alabama",
    "Alaska",
    "Arizona",
    "California",
    "Florida",
    "Georgia",
    "Illinois",
    "Maine",
    "Oregon",
    "Vermont"
  ),
])
fit <- hclust(dist(states), method = "average")
hchart(fit)
```

### Phylogenies

In the fan layout, radial distance measures branch length from the root.
With no lengths, each edge counts as one step. Use `layout = "rectangular"`
for a side-by-side reading of tip labels.

```{r phylo-fan, eval=requireNamespace("ape", quietly=TRUE)}
data("bird.families", package = "ape")
families <- c(
  "Rheidae",
  "Casuariidae",
  "Struthionidae",
  "Phasianidae",
  "Numididae",
  "Odontophoridae",
  "Anhimidae",
  "Dendrocygnidae",
  "Anatidae"
)
birds <- ape::keep.tip(bird.families, families)
hchart(birds)
```

## Networks {#igraph-package}

```{r}
library(igraph)
N <- 40

net <- sample_gnp(N, p = 2 / N)
wc <- cluster_walktrap(net)

V(net)$label <- seq(N)
V(net)$name <- paste("I'm #", seq(N))
V(net)$page_rank <- round(page_rank(net)$vector, 2)
V(net)$betweenness <- round(betweenness(net), 2)
V(net)$degree <- degree(net)
V(net)$size <- V(net)$degree
V(net)$comm <- as.vector(membership(wc))
V(net)$color <- colorize(membership(wc))

hchart(net, layout = layout_with_fr)
```
